precision road map's 10-bit ramp comes through it at less than half the
error it shows through `hevc` (T2; the figures are in
`designs/adr/precision.md`).

**AV1 (codec-export C1, C2, §11 CX-1, CX-2, CX-9, CX-10, CX-12, CX-13, CX-14).** One row after
`hevc_10bit`: `av1`, "AV1 (MP4)", MP4 with AAC, 10-bit Main 4:2:0 in every project,
even-sized, no alpha. Its picture is encoded by the bundled SVT-AV1 (CX-4), not
VideoToolbox, and the row says so in a field of its own, `writer`
(`"svt_av1"`); `avf_preset` is `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough`, a record
only, because AVFoundation still writes the container, so the row is routed
and sized as every AVFoundation row is and `avf_preset: null` keeps meaning
ImageIO. `rc_export_presets` gives the row and `av1_webm` (below) alone
`writer` and `encoder_speeds` (`["faster", "balanced", "smaller"]`), and their
resolved settings alone end with `writer` and `encoder_speed` — the override
(`faster`, `balanced`, `smaller`: SVT-AV1's presets 8, 6 and 4, CX-2),
`balanced` when absent; a word that is not one of the three is refused on
any row (`export encoder_speed must be "faster", "balanced" or "smaller",
not …`) and a speed on any other row is refused naming it (`{id} has no
encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm`). Every other row's settings
are the text they were. The frames: the reader's 64RGBAHalf frames are
scaled on the GPU (`MPSImageLanczosScale`) when the export size is not the
canvas — fitted with black bars, or filling a frame within a pixel of the
canvas's shape, G-33 (c) — and converted by `ExportI010.metal` to video-range
10-bit I010 through the picture's matrix (`ExportAV1Picture`, CX-14 (3): BT.709's
for `sdr`, BT.2020's for `hlg` and `pq`; Y = round(64 + 876·Y′), chroma
clamp(round(512 + 896·C′), 0, 1023) of the mean of each 2 × 2 block, premultiplied
RGB as it is, so a transparent canvas lands on black);
a serial encode queue owns the encoder (`ExportEncodePump`), with progress
counted by frames submitted, the cancel flag read before each read, send
and append, and the end of stream drained before `markAsFinished`. SVT-AV1
runs capped CRF (CX-13): the cap is `video_bitrate`, or HEVC's 0.07 bits
per pixel per frame when none is asked, set as `max_bit_rate`, and the CRF
is the one CX-13's calibration gives the speed at the cap's bits per pixel
per frame — matching or beating HEVC at that rate. The cap is soft (SVT's
default 50 % overshoot): a file usually averages far less than the rate,
and detailed footage was measured up to 1.254 × it; with a closed GOP and a
keyframe at least every 2 s (`intra_period_length` = ⌊2·fps⌋ − 1), and writes the
picture's primaries, transfer and matrix in video range into its sequence header
(CX-14 (4): `sdr` 1/1/1, `hlg` 9/18/9, `pq` 9/16/9). The
container bytes are the core's (`rc_av1_*`, CX-12 (4)): the `av1C` record
built from SVT's sequence header OBU, each packet's temporal delimiters
stripped, and the finished file's `ftyp` rewritten in place so `av01` is a
compatible brand (`isom mp41 mp42` → `isom av01 mp42`); a file whose `ftyp`
cannot take it fails the export. The packets go to a passthrough
`AVAssetWriterInput` whose format description holds the `av1C` and the same
colour tags (the `colr` box), one sample each; on `pq` alone HD-5's fixed HDR10
metadata is written twice, as SVT-AV1's HDR_MDCV and HDR_CLL metadata OBUs on
each KEY_FRAME and as the `av01` entry's `mdcv` and `clli` boxes from
`OutputTransform`'s two blobs, the same values (CX-14 (5)); the writer reads the sync
samples from the bitstream's key frames, so the pump attaches none.
SVT's own log goes through its callback: warnings and errors as `SVT-AV1: …`
lines in the system log, nothing else. **On an M1 or M2 Mac Frame Job cannot
play or re-import its own AV1 file, and QuickTime cannot either (CX-10):**
those Macs have no AV1 decoder, and #216's refusal stands.

**AV1 in WebM (codec-export C3, §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15).** `av1_webm`, "AV1
(WebM)", directly after `av1`: the same encoding — `writer` `svt_av1`, the
same `encoder_speeds`, CX-13's cap and CRF table, CX-14's I010, CICP and PQ
HDR10, one of the HDR rows, even-sized — in a WebM the core writes, with Opus
sound (container `webm`, `org.webmproject.webm`; `optimize_for_network`
defaults false and does nothing there, as on WAV; a speed on any other row is
refused `{id} has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and
av1_webm`). `Exporter.pipeline` gives it `ExportWebMWriter` (above), whose
video pump is `ExportEncodePump` into an `ExportWebMPacketSink` and whose
audio pump reads the mix, gains it, places it at its stamps (zeros for a
gap, a covered head cut: `ExportAudioEnd.align`), cuts it at the range
(`ExportAudioEnd`) and encodes it with AudioToolbox's Opus (`ExportOpusEncoder`:
48 kHz stereo, 20 ms packets behind a 960-frame FIFO fed by each buffer's
bytes, 192 kb/s by default or
`audio_bitrate`/the Quality tier snapped to the converter's rates, the
pre-skip `primeInfo.leadingFrames`). **The writer is the core's**
(`rc_webm_*`, `webm_writer.rs`): EBML DocType `webm` 4/2; a SeekHead patched
over a reserved Void; Info at millisecond timestamps with the duration and
"Frame Job"; track 1 `V_AV1` with the `av1C` as CodecPrivate, DefaultDuration
and Colour (the sequence header's CICP, Range 1, BitsPerChannel 10, and on
`pq` MaxCLL, MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata from `OutputTransform`'s blobs);
track 2 `A_OPUS` with OpusHead v1, CodecDelay round(pre-skip / 48 kHz) and an
80 ms SeekPreRoll; one chapter edition (`ExportChapter.partition`, language
`und`); block times rounded half up to the millisecond; a Cluster at each
video key (and before 32,767 ms), each key-started Cluster a CuePoint; the
Cues, the SeekHead and the Segment's size written at finish. The core
queues each declared track and writes the earliest head only while every
track not ended has one, so the two pumps never wait on each other (the
Opus track at worst, about 1.4 MB a minute, CX-15 (4)). **The tail:** the
encoder's finish feeds pre-skip frames of silence before its end of stream;
whole surplus packets are dropped and the last carries the rest as
DiscardPadding, so the decoded sound is #337's length exactly, and a
negative surplus fails the export (`The audio could not be encoded to its
exact length.`). **A composition with no audio track is a silent movie**:
no audio track in the file. A cancelled or failed export removes the file.
**One reader per output (CX-15 (2)):** the video composition output and the
audio mix output each have an `AVAssetReader` of their own, so neither read
can be starved by the other pump's stop, and each pump cancels its own reader
after its own last read (G-17's rule). G-17's starvation is closed for WebM
(F1–F3: a failure on either pump, or a cancel while the audio read is held,
ends the export within 10 s, and the readers' log line names a shared reader);
it stays accepted on `ExportWriter` (#378).

**Depth (§11 PR-1, PR-3).** The export reader reads the compositor's own
format, `64RGBAHalf` (`Compositor.outputPixelFormat`), and each row decides
what its encoder is handed (`ExportWriter.frameForm`, `ExportFrames` in
`ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`): `prores_422` and `prores_4444` take the
16-bit frames as they are (10-bit 4:2:2 and 12-bit 4:4:4:4 files), and so
does `hevc_10bit` (Main 10, 4:2:0, above), the
alpha rows straightened as above; `h264` (High, 8-bit) gets each frame
rounded to 8-bit BGRA (round(v·255)) in a pooled 32BGRA buffer, neither
straightened nor labelled, so its encoder input is what it was — H.264 fed
half-float frames measured worse on a ramp (8.80 steps RMS against 6.27);
`hevc` is rounded the same way, for the same reason (9.04 against 6.46),
and pinned to 8-bit Main (`kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main_AutoLevel`), because
VideoToolbox given no profile follows its input's format and the 16-bit
frames gave Main 10. `gif`, `apng` and image sequences are drawn by
`AVAssetImageGenerator` and keep §11 PR-4's rule. An APNG's frames carry
the BT.709 label every rendered frame's file carries, and a GIF's are left
as they are because a GIF carries no colour label (§11 PR-11).

**An HLG project (format 23, §11 HD-5, HD-13 (i), (j)).** The core's
resolver gives each of the three 10-bit rows — `hevc_10bit`, `prores_422`,
`prores_4444` — `"color": "hlg"` (`ExportSettings.color`), and `videoSettings`
then tags the file BT.2020 primaries, the HLG transfer and the BT.2020 matrix
(ffprobe `bt2020nc/arib-std-b67/bt2020`), HEVC with
`kVTHDRMetadataInsertionMode_None`, so VideoToolbox adds no Dolby Vision
configuration or RPU of its own (choice 5a). Every other video row is refused
in its own sentence — `h264 cannot carry an HLG project's picture; export it
as hevc_10bit, prores_422 or prores_4444` — until H-3's SDR version; an audio
row is unchanged, and every SDR project's settings are the text they were.
`render_frame` and Save Frame… read every frame of an HLG project through the
reader (`DeepVideoFrame.reads`, whatever the format) and label it
`itur_2100_HLG` (`FrameWriter.hlgSpace`, kept by `labelled`): a 16-bit PNG
that ImageIO writes with a `cICP` chunk 9/18/0/1, or a 10-bit HEIC; JPEG is
refused (`JPEG cannot carry an HLG project's picture; save the frame as PNG or
HEIC`). The eyedropper and Pick from Canvas read such a frame relabelled sRGB
(`FrameWriter.pickable`), at its code values.

**The deliverables (hdr H-3, §11 HD-4, HD-5, HD-14).** H-2's refusals are
gone. The override `dynamic_range` (`"hlg"`, `"pq"` or `"sdr"`; any other
value refused, `export dynamic_range must be "hlg", "pq" or "sdr", not …`) is
read by `export_overrides.rs` and resolved per row by `dynamic_range.rs`
(`Project::deliverable`): an HLG project's HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`,
`av1_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, CX-14 (2), CX-15) default to `hlg` and take all three;
its other video rows (`h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `gif`, `apng`) write
`sdr`, refusing `hlg` and `pq` (`{id} is 8-bit and writes the SDR version;
export dynamic_range "{x}" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444`); an SDR project refuses `hlg` and `pq` (`dynamic_range "{x}"
needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first`) and takes `sdr` as
nothing; an audio row reads it and ignores it. The settings' `color` names
the picture (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`) in an HLG project only, and
`rc_export_presets` marks the five HDR rows `"hdr": true`
(`ExportPreset.carriesHDR`). `Exporter.export` publishes the asked options
`.delivering(settings)`, so `pq` and `sdr` reach the recipe as the option
`dynamic_range` and the output pass (§7.5) draws them; the composition is
labelled to match. `videoSettings` tags `sdr` BT.709 ×3 (today's), `hlg` as

content.content:
the reason the whole design exists — two writers would make the chapter
track, the explicit bitrates and the output size conditional on which one
happened to run, and leave two answers to "what did the file end up as".
`ExportWriter` reads the composition through an `AVAssetReader` and writes
video, audio and a chapter track (an `AVAssetWriterInput` text track
associated `AVTrackAssociationTypeChapterList`), reporting `progress` on
the same timer the sheet already polled. GIF and APNG take the ImageIO
path instead, frame by frame over `Exporter.renderFrame`. **The one
exception is WebM (§11 CX-15 (2)):** `AVAssetWriter` writes no WebM, so
`Exporter.pipeline` sends a `webm` container to `ExportWebMWriter`, a second
`ExportPipeline` that is `ExportWriter`'s WebM half and nothing more — the
same reader outputs (`ExportWriter.videoReadOutput` / `audioReadOutput`), the
same `ExportEncodePump`, gain, #337 end, chapter partition
(`ExportChapter.partition`), size and rates — so each of those is still one
decision, and only the container differs.

**Quality.** `video_bitrate` and `audio_bitrate` are overrides in bits per
second, strictly positive; a zero, a negative, a fraction or a non-number
is an error naming the value. No preset carries a default and neither key

the reason the whole design exists — two writers would make the chapter
track, the explicit bitrates and the output size conditional on which one
happened to run, and leave two answers to "what did the file end up as".

video, audio and a chapter track (an `AVAssetWriterInput` text track

decision, and only the container differs.

# 7.8 Export

Presets (`rc_export_presets`), in menu order, are ENCODINGS — a container
and a codec, with no size of their own: `h264` H.264 (MP4), `hevc` HEVC
(MP4), `hevc_alpha` HEVC with Alpha (MOV), `hevc_10bit` HEVC 10-bit (MP4),
`av1` AV1 (MP4), `av1_webm` AV1 (WebM), `prores_422` ProRes 422 (MOV), `prores_4444` ProRes 4444 (MOV), `audio_m4a` Audio only (M4A),
`audio_wav` Audio only (WAV), `audio_aiff` Audio only (AIFF), `gif`
Animated GIF, `apng` Animated PNG. The size is a separate choice whose
default is the document's own size, so a 1440p or a vertical project does
not come out at 1920 × 1080 because a row said so; the two image formats
are the exception and carry the cap argued below. **The first row of each
list is the default.** The export sheet opens on the remembered choice
(`ExportChoice.remembered`, written on Export or Add to Queue), and on
`h264` with its Size popup on the first row only when none is remembered;
the Size rows are `rc_export_sizes(project, preset)`, which lists
the sizes offered for that document and format: the document's size
(`document` — "Document size", not "source size": §4.3's source size is a
media item's, and this row renders at the canvas), or for an image format
its cap (`preset`) with the document's size second; then the standard
sizes fitted to the document's aspect, largest first — `2160p` (named 4K),
`1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`. The number is the SHORT edge, because "1080p
ultrawide" is 2560 × 1080 and "1080p vertical" is 1080 × 1920 — the short
edge is the number people mean — and the long edge is the document's,
scaled to match and rounded to the nearest even integer, since H.264 and
HEVC need even dimensions and a size the writer would quietly change is
not one the sheet may offer. The same holds for the Document row and for
any size asked for (§11 G-33): on the rows that need even dimensions —
every row AVFoundation writes but `prores_4444` — an odd edge is resolved
one pixel SMALLER, which is the size the writer always wrote, so on a
canvas with an odd edge that row's numbers are the canvas evened and its
name is "Document (even)"; `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` keep an odd
edge, and theirs stays "Document size". A row may repeat an earlier row's
numbers —
a 1920 × 1080 document's `1080p` is its own size — and is listed anyway,
because an id is the `export` tool's vocabulary and has to mean the same
thing on every document; the sheet hides a row whose numbers an earlier
row already has, keeping the name that says more. On an image format
every row's numbers are the canvas fitted inside that box, never upscaled
(below). The audio-only preset lists the same rows as `h264` and the sheet
disables the control. The agent's `export` takes the same ids in its
`size`, or an explicit `[width, height]` (the sheet's "Custom…").
`rc_export_settings` resolves a preset plus overrides (size, fps, range =
whole or in/out, `optimize_for_network`, the two bitrates below, the two
loudness figures below them and `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s `encoder_speed`) to
concrete settings, no size override meaning the preset's cap where it has
one and the canvas otherwise — and to the size the file will have: the
width and height it answers are evened as above on the rows that need it
and fitted on the image formats, whether they came from the canvas, a row
or a custom size. Each preset AVFoundation can write still
carries an `AVAssetExportSession` preset name
(`AVAssetExportPresetHighestQuality`, `…HEVCHighestQuality`,
`…HEVCHighestQualityWithAlpha`, `…AppleProRes422LPCM`,
`…AppleProRes4444LPCM`, `…AppleM4A`, and `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s
`…Passthrough`) — that
mapping is what names the
codec and tier, and `avf_preset: null` is how a preset says AVFoundation
cannot write it at all. Since phase 5 the field means **only** that: the
name is a record, not an instruction, because `null` is what routes an
export to the ImageIO writer and AVFoundation has no `AVAssetExportPreset`
for LPCM, so `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` repeat `audio_m4a`'s name — the

content.content:
# Exporting

Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.

## Opening the export sheet

Choose **File ▸ Export…** (⌘E), or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty. An export always writes the whole top-level timeline, even when you are working inside a nest.

The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not to the project, so every document's sheet opens on it. A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document that has no range.

## The controls

From top to bottom:

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Preset** | Applies a saved set of choices (see [Presets](#presets)). The gear beside it saves and deletes presets. | Custom |
| **Format** | The encoding: container and codec together. | H.264 (MP4) |
| **Dynamic Range** | Shown only in an HDR (HLG) project. See [HDR projects](#hdr-projects). | HDR (HLG) |
| **Speed** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Speed](#speed). | Balanced |
| **Size** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. | The format's first row |
| **Frame rate** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. | Project rate |
| **Quality** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. | Format default |
| **Loudness** | **Off**, a loudness target, or **Custom…** with a LUFS field. | Off |
| **Range** | **Whole project**, or **In/out range** when one is set. | Whole project |
| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the picture. | Off |

Under the controls, a readout line describes the file and a footnote names the codec, the container and the rates the file will use. Every number they show is the size, rate and duration the file will actually have.

- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`.
## Transparency

A canvas whose background is transparent (the **Background** row in the Document tab's Appearance section; see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#appearance)) keeps its transparency only in **ProRes 4444**, **HEVC with Alpha** and **Animated PNG**. When the format carries an alpha channel, the footnote ends in "alpha". Every other format composites the picture onto black. A GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so it is not one of the three.

While the canvas background is transparent, the Document tab says how many formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 3 export formats." These are the three formats above.

## Chapters

Chapter markers on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)) become chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter's name is the marker's name, or "Chapter *n*" for an unnamed one. A range export keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file, and the chapter already running when the range starts opens the file. WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG have no chapters.

MP4 and M4A files are written with their index at the front, so a player can start before the whole file has downloaded.

## What an export includes

- **The same picture and sound as the preview.** The export uses the same composition and the same compositor. View-only settings never reach it: Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version, Show Selection, safe areas and the scopes.
- **Speed ramps and Keep pitch off.** An export waits for the rendered audio of every speed ramp, and of every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, to finish before it writes, and shows "Preparing…" meanwhile. That sound is never exported silent (see [Speed](speed.md)). If it cannot be rendered, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …".
- **Missing media.** A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence instead of failing the export.
- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Captions** are ordinary text clips, so they are always burned into the picture. To write a separate subtitle file, use **File ▸ Export Captions…** (see [Captions](captions.md)).

## For agents

`export` mirrors **Export…** with **Add to Queue**: it checks the request, puts the job in the Export Queue and answers at once with `{export_id, path, status}`. Status is `queued` or `running`.

| Argument | The sheet's control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` (required) | Format | `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif`, `apng`. |
| `path` (required) | Save panel | The folder must exist. An existing file is replaced. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and a different known media extension is replaced: `cut.mov` with `h264` writes `cut.mp4`. Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `size` | Size | `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (GIF and APNG only), or `[width, height]`. |
| `range` | Range | `project` (default) or `in_out`. Refused when there is no in/out range. |
| `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate` | Quality | Bits per second. On `av1` and `av1_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft cap the file usually stays under. `audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate. |
| `loudness_lufs` | Loudness | −70 to 0. |
| `peak_dbtp` | (fixed at −1 on the sheet) | −20 to 0. Refused without `loudness_lufs`. |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Burn in timecode | |
| `dynamic_range` | Dynamic Range | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. |
| `encoder_speed` | Speed | `faster`, `balanced` (default) or `smaller`. `av1` and `av1_webm` only; refused on every other format. |

There is no frame-rate argument. An agent's export uses the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own.

Every refusal comes back from `export` itself, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing folder, an empty timeline, or a graphic that does not compile.

- `export_status {export_id}` answers the job's row without waiting: `queued`, `running` (with `progress` from 0 to 1 and `phase`), `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Call it again after a pause until the job finishes.
  - Every answer has `path` and `elapsed` (seconds).

toolUseResult.stdout:
# Exporting

Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.

## Opening the export sheet

Choose **File ▸ Export…** (⌘E), or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty. An export always writes the whole top-level timeline, even when you are working inside a nest.

The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not to the project, so every document's sheet opens on it. A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document that has no range.

## The controls

From top to bottom:

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Preset** | Applies a saved set of choices (see [Presets](#presets)). The gear beside it saves and deletes presets. | Custom |
| **Format** | The encoding: container and codec together. | H.264 (MP4) |
| **Dynamic Range** | Shown only in an HDR (HLG) project. See [HDR projects](#hdr-projects). | HDR (HLG) |
| **Speed** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Speed](#speed). | Balanced |
| **Size** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. | The format's first row |
| **Frame rate** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. | Project rate |
| **Quality** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. | Format default |
| **Loudness** | **Off**, a loudness target, or **Custom…** with a LUFS field. | Off |
| **Range** | **Whole project**, or **In/out range** when one is set. | Whole project |
| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the picture. | Off |

Under the controls, a readout line describes the file and a footnote names the codec, the container and the rates the file will use. Every number they show is the size, rate and duration the file will actually have.

- **Readout:** `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` (size, frame rate, duration). For the audio-only formats it reads `Audio only · 00:01:12.200`. For GIF and APNG it adds the frame count: `· 360 frames, no audio`.
## Transparency

A canvas whose background is transparent (the **Background** row in the Document tab's Appearance section; see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md#appearance)) keeps its transparency only in **ProRes 4444**, **HEVC with Alpha** and **Animated PNG**. When the format carries an alpha channel, the footnote ends in "alpha". Every other format composites the picture onto black. A GIF can show a pixel as fully transparent but has no partial transparency, so it is not one of the three.

While the canvas background is transparent, the Document tab says how many formats will keep it: "Transparent — kept by 3 export formats." These are the three formats above.

## Chapters

Chapter markers on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)) become chapters in MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter's name is the marker's name, or "Chapter *n*" for an unnamed one. A range export keeps the chapters inside the range, with their times counted from the start of the file, and the chapter already running when the range starts opens the file. WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG have no chapters.

MP4 and M4A files are written with their index at the front, so a player can start before the whole file has downloaded.

## What an export includes

- **The same picture and sound as the preview.** The export uses the same composition and the same compositor. View-only settings never reach it: Preview Quality, Show Ungraded, Show SDR Version, Show Selection, safe areas and the scopes.
- **Speed ramps and Keep pitch off.** An export waits for the rendered audio of every speed ramp, and of every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, to finish before it writes, and shows "Preparing…" meanwhile. That sound is never exported silent (see [Speed](speed.md)). If it cannot be rendered, the export fails with "Clip *n*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …".
- **Missing media.** A clip whose file is missing still exports, showing its slate and with no sound. An audio track none of whose clips can be read is written as silence instead of failing the export.
- **Graphics.** An export draws the graphics as they were when it was asked for, even if a module is saved again mid-export. If a graphic in the range, or in a nest the range reaches, does not compile or has no module, the export does not start and names the graphic. If a graphic fails while the file is being written, the export stops at that frame, names the graphic, and leaves no file. See [Graphics](graphics.md).
- **Captions** are ordinary text clips, so they are always burned into the picture. To write a separate subtitle file, use **File ▸ Export Captions…** (see [Captions](captions.md)).

`export` mirrors **Export…** with **Add to Queue**: it checks the request, puts the job in the Export Queue and answers at once with `{export_id, path, status}`. Status is `queued` or `running`.

| Argument | The sheet's control | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` (required) | Format | `h264`, `hevc`, `hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif`, `apng`. |
| `path` (required) | Save panel | The folder must exist. An existing file is replaced. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and a different known media extension is replaced: `cut.mov` with `h264` writes `cut.mp4`. Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
| `size` | Size | `document`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p`, `preset` (GIF and APNG only), or `[width, height]`. |

| `loudness_lufs` | Loudness | −70 to 0. |
| `peak_dbtp` | (fixed at −1 on the sheet) | −20 to 0. Refused without `loudness_lufs`. |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Burn in timecode | |
| `dynamic_range` | Dynamic Range | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. |
| `encoder_speed` | Speed | `faster`, `balanced` (default) or `smaller`. `av1` and `av1_webm` only; refused on every other format. |

There is no frame-rate argument. An agent's export uses the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own.

content.content:
Every refusal — a bad argument, a missing folder, a graphic that does not
compile — comes back from `export` itself, before anything is queued. A
failure while writing comes back from `export_status` as `failed` with its
reason; a graphic that fails during the export stops it, leaving no file,
and the reason names the graphic and the frame.

`export` takes `preset` and `path`, plus `size`, `range` (`project` or
`in_out`), `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate`, `loudness_lufs`, `peak_dbtp`,
`burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range` and `encoder_speed`. The presets are `h264`, `hevc`,
`hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`,
`audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` and `apng`. There is no frame-rate
argument: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and
25 fps for `apng`. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the
format's extension is added when the path has none. `peak_dbtp` without
`loudness_lufs` is refused. `dynamic_range` `hlg` or `pq` is refused outside
`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`, and in an SDR project.
`encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`) is `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s
alone and is refused on every other preset; the done answer names it. On both,
`video_bitrate` is a soft cap: the file usually comes in well under it, and
very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over it. What each option means is in [Export](export.md).

## Reading the project: get_project

`get_project` answers the whole project as JSON, the same document every op
94:**Export.** H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), AV1 in MP4 or WebM
on its own or beside the screen as a corner talking head; or a
microphone-only voice-over.
→ [Screen recording](docs/guide/screen-recording.md)

**Export.** H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), AV1 in MP4 or WebM
(10-bit, with HDR, from its own encoder built in, at three speeds; Opus sound
in the WebM), ProRes 422 and 4444,
M4A, WAV, AIFF, GIF and animated PNG; loudness targets, presets, an Export
Queue that runs while you edit, and single frames as stills.
→ [Exporting](docs/guide/export.md)

**SE-17 — An AV1 export plays and comes back in**
- **Do:** on a Mac with an M3 or later, export a project with sound and motion as AV1 (MP4) at each Speed; play each file in QuickTime Player; import one into a new Frame Job project and play it.
- **Expect:** each file plays in QuickTime with its picture and sound in sync and no corruption, and Frame Job imports it, previews it and plays its sound in sync.
- **Answer:** does the AV1 export play in QuickTime and come back into Frame Job, picture and sound in sync?
- **Source:** #377, codec-export C1 (spec §11 CX-10, CX-12).

**SE-18 — An AV1 (WebM) export plays in the browsers and comes back in**
- **Do:** 1. Export a project with sound, motion and two chapter markers as **AV1 (WebM)** from File ▸ Export…. 2. Open the file in Chrome and in Firefox, play it through and scrub it. 3. On a Mac with an M3 or later, import it into a new Frame Job project, put it on the timeline and play it.
- **Expect:** both browsers play the picture and the Opus sound in sync to the end, with no corruption, no click at the start or the end, and seeking lands where it is asked; on the M3 or later Frame Job imports it, previews it and plays its sound in sync.
- **Answer:** does the WebM play in Chrome and Firefox, and come back into Frame Job on an M3 or later, picture and sound in sync?
- **Source:** #377, codec-export C3 (spec §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15); `tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py` reads the file through ffprobe, ffmpeg and an EBML walk on an M2 Max, which cannot decode AV1, not how a browser plays it.

**HDR-2 — An HLG project's exports in QuickTime Player and on an iPhone**
- **Do:** 1. In an HLG project (Document tab ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)) with an iPhone HLG clip of a face, a white text title over it and a short Frame Job screen recording after it, open File ▸ Export… and read the Dynamic Range row on `hevc_10bit`, then on `h264`. 2. Export `hevc_10bit` and `prores_422` (Dynamic Range: HDR (HLG)) and `h264` (the SDR version). 3. Open the three side by side in QuickTime Player on the XDR display, then AirDrop the `hevc_10bit` and `h264` files to an iPhone and open them in Photos. 4. Turn View ▸ Show SDR Version on and compare the preview with the `h264` file.

**HDR-3 — An HDR10 (PQ) export**
- **Do:** 1. In the same HLG project, export `hevc_10bit` with Dynamic Range: HDR10 (PQ). 2. Open it in QuickTime Player on the XDR display beside the HLG `hevc_10bit` export. 3. Open it in a player that shows HDR10 metadata (for example IINA's or VLC's media information, or MediaInfo).
- **Expect:** the PQ file looks like the HLG one on the XDR display (the same highlights, the title at reference white); the metadata reads a mastering display of P3 D65 primaries at 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0 (unknown), and no Dolby Vision.

**HDR-4 — A real HDR10 file mastered above 1,000 cd/m²**
- **Do:** 1. Import an HDR10 PQ file whose mastering peak is above 1,000 cd/m² and whose stated peak you know (a Resolve export, a camera's HDR10 recording or a downloaded HDR10 sample; ideally one at 4,000 cd/m²) into an ordinary (SDR) project of its own. 2. Select its row in the Media tab and read the HDR10 section. 3. Look at its brightest part — a sky, a lamp, a specular highlight — in the preview, paused and playing, and in a saved frame (File ▸ Save Frame…), side by side with the same file in QuickTime Player. 4. Set Peak to 1,000 cd/m², look at the same highlights again, then press Use File's. 5. Undo and redo each step once. 6. **HDR-6 — The scopes on real HDR footage**
- **Do:** 1. In an HLG project (Document tab ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)), put a real iPhone HLG clip of a face against a bright sky, a white text title over it, and a short Frame Job screen recording after it. 2. Turn View ▸ Scopes on and pick each scope in turn in both slots — Waveform, Parade, Vectorscope, Histogram — paused on the face with the title, then on the recording; look in both appearances. 3. Turn View ▸ Show SDR Version on and look at every scope again; turn it off. 4. Turn View ▸ Show Ungraded on and off with a grade on the clip. 5. Open an ordinary (SDR) project with its own footage and look at its scopes.
- **Expect:** the waveform's and parade's labels read 0, 10, 51, 203 and 1000, each legible beside its line in both appearances, "1000" not clipped by the slot's edge; the title's trace sits on the dashed 75 % line (203 cd/m²), the sky's highlights above it, and only truly clipped highlights get red marks at the top; the captions read "HLG · cd/m²" over the waveform and parade and "Rec. 2100 HLG" over the vectorscope and histogram; on the vectorscope the face sits near the skin line and the six target boxes lie on the hues they name; with Show SDR Version on every scope turns to its Rec. 709 reading ("Rec. 709 · encoded", labels 0/50/100, no dashed line) and the title sits near the top; Show Ungraded keeps the HLG scale and shows the clip without its grade; the SDR project's scopes look exactly as they did before.
- **Source:** the HDR road map's H-4 (spec §11 HD-8, HD-15: the HLG project's scopes, #277); `tools/proof/hdr_proof.py`'s SW–SP rows and P8 measure synthetic ramps, bars and offscreen bitmaps, not how the panel reads on real footage.

**HDR-7 — An iPhone HDR photo**
- **Do:** 1. Copy a photo from the iPhone 18 Pro (an HDR HEIC, default Camera settings) into a new project, and look at it on the XDR display beside the same photo in Photos. 2. Set the Document tab's Dynamic Range to HDR (HLG) and look again. 3. Export `hevc_10bit` and open it in QuickTime Player beside the preview. 4. Turn View ▸ Show SDR Version on, then off. 5. Undo back to SDR and look at the photo, its timeline filmstrip and its Media-tab thumbnail. 6. Repeat 1–5 with a photo from iOS 17 or older if one is at hand.

- **Do:** 1. On a Mac with an M3 or later chip and an XDR display, in an HLG project (Document tab ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)) with an iPhone HLG clip of a face and a white text title over it, export **AV1 (MP4)** twice from File ▸ Export…: Dynamic Range HDR (HLG), then HDR10 (PQ); then **AV1 (WebM)** the same two ways. 2. Export the same project as **HEVC 10-bit (MP4)** at HDR (HLG). 3. Open the three MP4 files side by side in QuickTime Player, and the two WebM files in Chrome. 4. Open the AV1 HDR10 files in a player that shows HDR10 metadata (for example MediaInfo).
- **Expect:** every AV1 file plays, and their highlights glow above the interface's white as the `hevc_10bit` file's do, with the title at reference white and no shift in colour; each AV1 HDR10 file's metadata reads a mastering display of P3 D65 primaries at 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0, HD-5's fixed values.

## Codec export C3 — AV1 in WebM, with Opus (`webm_export_proof.py` Z1, W1–W13, S4, R1, F1–F3, P1–P5, A1–A5; thirteen mutants; `export_offset_proof.py` E38–E40; spec §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15)

The `av1_webm` row: `av1`'s picture (the same `ExportEncodePump` and SVT-AV1) and Opus sound
from AudioToolbox (`ExportOpusEncoder`), written into a WebM by the core's own writer
(`rc_webm_*`: `webm_ebml.rs`, `webm_layout.rs`, `webm_writer.rs`) through `ExportWebMWriter`,
the second `ExportPipeline`.

```
python3 tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH]          # every row
python3 tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py --probe                             # P1–P5, A1–A5 alone, no app

the count alone cannot see it); W3 A5's key rule, the key flags read from the file's blocks
(ffprobe's for AV1 in Matroska are ffmpeg's parser's, from the bitstream); W4 the walk (the Segment's size, the

- **(a) Matroska's HDR10 fields** (RFC 9559's Colour element): MaxCLL 0x55BC and MaxFALL
    0x55BD (unsigned integers, cd/m²) and MasteringMetadata 0x55D0, whose children are floats —
    PrimaryRChromaticityX/Y 0x55D1/0x55D2, G 0x55D3/0x55D4, B 0x55D5/0x55D6, the white point
    0x55D7/0x55D8, LuminanceMax 0x55D9 and LuminanceMin 0x55DA (cd/m²). The core reads them with
    the Colour element and `rc_container_describe` reports them (the video's `mdcv_hex`,
    `clli_hex`, and the Colour's `transfer`, `primaries` and `matrix` codes, each null when
    absent). The copy's format description carries them as HD-12's two blobs **only when the
    Colour's transfer is 16** (PQ), so an SDR or untagged copy gains nothing, and HD-12's route 1
    reads them unchanged:
    - `MasteringDisplayColorVolume`, 24 bytes, written when 0x55D0 is present: the primaries in
      ST 2086's and SEI 137's order G, B, R, then the white point, each x and y a big-endian u16
      of round(c·50000) clamped to 0…50000; then the maximum and minimum luminance, each a
      big-endian u32 of round(L·10000) clamped to the u32's range (NaN or negative → 0). An
      absent child is 0.
    - `ContentLightLevelInfo`, 4 bytes, written when MaxCLL or MaxFALL is present: MaxCLL then
      MaxFALL, each a big-endian u16 clamped to 65535, an absent one 0.
  - **(b) The PQ label.** A copy whose Colour's transfer is 16 is labelled PQ in its format
    description: `TransferFunction` SMPTE ST 2084, and `ColorPrimaries` and `YCbCrMatrix` from
    `CVColorPrimariesGetStringForIntegerCodePoint` and `CVYCbCrMatrixGetStringForIntegerCodePoint`
    when the Colour names them and Core Video maps the code. No other copy's description changes.
  - **(c) AV1.** The description's two extensions first (HD-12's route 1); else the stream (AV1
    §5.3, §5.8; AV1-ISOBMFF §2.3): the `av1C`'s configOBUs (bytes 4 on, when byte 0 is 0x81, the
    marker and version 1; else none), then the first sample with data. Every OBU is walked: the
    type is the header's bits 6–3, an extension byte is skipped, `obu_size` is a leb128 of at
    most 8 bytes when `obu_has_size_field` is set, else the OBU is the rest of the bytes. An
    OBU_METADATA (type 5) is read by its leb128 `metadata_type`: 1 HDR_CLL (`max_cll` a
    big-endian u16, 4 bytes or more) and 2 HDR_MDCV (`luminance_max` a big-endian u32 at payload
    bytes 16–19 in 24.8 fixed point, 24 bytes or more), the first of each kept, the config's
    before the sample's. The maximum is whole cd/m² as (v + 128) / 256 in 64 bits, clamped to
    10,000, 0 no reading; MaxCLL as it stands, 0 absent, clamped to 10,000. MaxCLL first, else
    the mastering maximum, as HD-12. The core's pure `hdr10.rs` reads it through one export,

STOP: V10 as the spec states it cannot pass without re-litigating spec §11 HD-18 (b). Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` re-imports with the wrong YCbCr matrix: it is decoded as BT.601, not BT.709. A render of the imported media at 3 s differs from the source project's by R/G/B 11.83/0.79/5.65 against V10's bound of 8/255. HD-18 (b) says a WebM/Matroska copy gets colour labels only when its Colour's transfer is 16 (PQ), and HD-19 (b) extends that to HLG: "No other copy's description changes." So `ContainerRewrapWriter` writes no `YCbCrMatrix` for an SDR copy. AVFoundation then picks the matrix by frame size, and a picture this small gets BT.601. The encoder and the file are right (V1, V4, V8 read BT.709 everywhere), and the same check at 1280 × 720 passes. A ruling is needed before C4 can finish; options are listed below.

# C4 — implementation notes (vp9_webm)

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs`, branch `codecs`. Nothing committed.

## What happened with V10 (the STOP)

- **The row as specced.** V10 imports V1's file (640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm`). It puts the media alone in a 640 × 360 project and renders t = 3 s with `render_frame`, then compares each RGB channel's mean absolute difference with A1's project rendered at 3 s. The bound is 8/255.
- **What it read on Debug.** R 11.826, G 0.782, B 5.647. The two durations and sizes were right: 5.013 s, 640 × 360, with audio.
- **Sample pixels** (row 100, the colour bars). Each pair is source, then import:
  - cyan (0,255,255) → (23,255,255)
  - magenta (255,0,255) → (236,0,247)
  - green (0,255,1) → (20,255,9)
  - red (255,0,0) → (235,0,2)
- **The cause.** BT.709 cyan (Y′ 0.7874, Cr′ −0.5) decoded with BT.601's 1.402 gives R = 0.0864, which is 22. That is the import's 23, so the copy is being decoded as BT.601.
- **The control.** The same round trip at 1280 × 720 (a scratch script, same app, same AV.mov) reads R/G/B 0.526/0.157/0.296. Only the SD-sized picture is affected, which fits AVFoundation choosing the matrix by size for an unlabelled description.
- **Why I did not fix it.**
  - `ContainerRewrapWriter.labels` is reached only from `pqLabels` and `hlgLabels`. Its comment and spec §11 HD-18 (b) say "No other copy's description changes."
  - Labelling SDR copies by their Colour (primaries 1 and matrix 1 → BT.709) would change a §11 decision.
  - It would touch every SDR WebM/MKV import, not only Frame Job's own files.
  - Moving V10 to an HD canvas would make the row pass while the defect stays. That defect is any SD BT.709 VP9 WebM, from Frame Job or from ffmpeg, previewing with BT.601 colours.
- **Options for the orchestrator / owner:**
  - (a) A new §11 entry amending HD-18 (b): an SDR copy whose Colour names its primaries and matrix gets `ColorPrimaries` and `YCbCrMatrix`, and perhaps the 709 transfer, in its description. This is a change to `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift`, plus re-running the import proofs (`container_import_proof.py`, `codec_import_proof.py`, `hdr_proof.py`'s H7 rows). V10 then passes as written.
  - (b) Accept the defect, file it as an issue, and move V10's render comparison to a 1280 × 720 project (measured 0.53/0.16/0.30). The import half stays at 640 × 360.
  - (c) Keep V10 at 640 × 360 and compare luma alone. This hides nothing about the encoder, but it says nothing about colour either.

## What was built before the STOP

- **Order.** CX-16 was written first, then the core, then Swift, then the instruments and documents.
- **Decision.** `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md` has CX-16 (1)–(9) and the risks.
  - (8), the calibration, says "filled in after the run" and is still empty.
  - "Amended by CX-16" sits under CX-8, and after CX-15 (3) for CX-15 (1)–(3), as one paragraph.
  - `hdr.md` has "Amended by CX-16" under HD-5's row list and HD-14 (c).
  - `11-decisions/README.md` has the file row's text and a CX-16 row, and marks CX-8, CX-15, HD-5 and HD-14 "amended by CX-16". Its Lines cells and `designs/spec/README.md`'s are **not yet updated**: (8) is still to grow. `spec_index_proof.py` will fail until they are.
- **Core** (no format bump, no new `rc_*`):
  - `Writer::Libvpx` and `Writer::takes_speed`.
  - The `vp9_webm` row: `PRESETS: [Preset; 14]`, its JSON `hdr` and `writer: "libvpx"`, no `encoder_speeds`.
  - `takes_encoder_speed` is `writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)`. `to_json` emits `encoder_speeds` only where speeds apply.
  - The settings emit `writer` on every writer row and `encoder_speed` only on the AV1 rows.
  - `HDR_ROWS` has six rows, and the 8-bit sentence names `vp9_webm`.
  - `webm_layout.rs`: an optional `codec_private_hex`, and the four refusals in the spec's words.
  - `webm_ebml::video_entry(codec_id, Option<private>, …)`.
  - The header's presets, settings and webm paragraphs.
  - Sizes: `export_table.rs` 582, `webm_ebml.rs` 401, `webm_layout.rs` 222.
- **Core tests:**
  - New `export_vp9.rs` (6 tests) and `webm_writer_vp9.rs` (4: Profile 0 SDR and Profile 2 PQ through `Container`, which reads `vp09`, the synthesized `vpcC` profile and depth, and MDCV/CLLI; the walk finds no CodecPrivate and the Colour codes, bits and mastering; key flags in the walk and the reader).
  - `common/webm.rs` gains the hand-built VP9 keyframe and inter-frame headers, `vp9_layout` and `write_vp9`.
  - Updated: `webm_writer_refusals.rs` (V_HEVC, V_VP9 with a private, an absent V_AV1 private, 12 bits), `export.rs` (14 rows, `writer` alone on `vp9_webm`), `export_av1.rs`, `export_size.rs` (11 even-sized rows), `dynamic_range.rs` (six), `canvas_output.rs`.
- **Swift:**
  - `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h`, quoted-included by the bridging header.
  - `ExportVideoEncoder.swift`: the protocol, `ExportEncodedPacket` and `ExportRateTable`.
  - `ExportVP9Encoder.swift` (238 lines).
  - `SVTAV1Encoder` conforms: `Packet` is a typealias of the shared packet, `containerBytes` strips the TDs, and `crf` goes through `ExportRateTable` with the same values (P1 confirmed them).
  - `ExportEncodePump`: `av1Writer`/`vp9Writer`, `webmCodec`, an optional `formatDescription`, the encoder chosen by `writer`. The out-of-order sentence names the encoder.
  - `ExportI010`: `bitDepth` and the `framejob_export_i420` kernel.
  - `ExportAV1Picture.cicp`, and `ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec`.
  - The WebM writer's guard and layout call; the MP4 sink's optional format; `ExporterWriter`'s one identifier.
  - `ExportPreset.writer` and `Applies.softCap`, `codecFactor` taking `vp9`, and `ExportSheetResolve.swift` line 477.
- **Not done yet** (blocked behind the calibration and the STOP):
  - `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`'s descriptions are **not edited yet**. They wait for VP9's measured maximum.
  - The `designs/codec-export.md` C4 record and `tools/proof/README.md`'s C4 section are not written.
- **Documents:**
  - Spec §7.8 (the VP9 paragraph, the preset list, the deliverables), §7.1, §7.4 (a new encoders row and the WebM row), §7.10, §7.9a.
  - The guide's `export.md`, `hdr-and-color.md` and `mcp.md`, and `README.md`.
  - `docs/manual-checks.md`: SE-19, and `vp9_webm` added to HDR-2's list and HDR-8.
  - The guide pages and `mcp.md` still hold the literal placeholder **`VP9MAX`**: three places in `docs/guide/export.md` and one in `docs/guide/mcp.md`. The calibration's measured maximum cap share replaces it.
- **Proofs:**
  - New `tools/proof/vp9_export_proof.py` (Z1, V1–V11, S1, P1, R1–R3, nine mutants) and `vp9_rate_probe.swift`.
  - `export_offset_proof.py` gets E41 and E42.
  - Sentence constants updated in `av1_export_proof.py` (H5), `hdr_proof.py` (DR) and `hevc_alpha_proof.py` (`B6_SIZE`).
  - `av1_export_proof.py`'s `av1-not-hdr` anchor is re-pointed to the six-row, multi-line `HDR_ROWS`. Every other anchor in it and in `webm_export_proof.py` is still found once (checked). The re-anchored mutant has **not** been re-run.
- **Calibration instrument.** `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf_vp9.py` (gitignored), with modes `spike`, `owner [--reuse] --depth 8|10 --start {…}` and `table`.

## Deviations so far (beyond the STOP)

- **Mutant row lists** (`vp9_export_proof.py`), from reading which rows each mutation reaches. Only `vp9-not-hdr` follows the spec; the mutants were not yet run.
  - `sdr-at-10-bits` names V1 **and V8**: V8's `sdr` case reads the same profile and depth.
  - `transfer-unlabelled` mutates `ExportAV1Picture.cicp`'s HLG and PQ transfers to 2, not every transfer. Otherwise V1's SDR Colour fails too. It stays V8 alone.

STOP: V10 as the spec states it cannot pass without re-litigating spec §11 HD-18 (b). Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` re-imports with the wrong YCbCr matrix: it is decoded as BT.601, not BT.709. A render of the imported media at 3 s differs from the source project's by R/G/B 11.83/0.79/5.65 against V10's bound of 8/255. HD-18 (b) says a WebM/Matroska copy gets colour labels only when its Colour's transfer is 16 (PQ), and HD-19 (b) extends that to HLG: "No other copy's description changes." So `ContainerRewrapWriter` writes no `YCbCrMatrix` for an SDR copy. AVFoundation then picks the matrix by frame size, and a picture this small gets BT.601. The encoder and the file are right (V1, V4, V8 read BT.709 everywhere), and the same check at 1280 × 720 passes. A ruling is needed before C4 can finish; options are listed below.

# C4 — implementation notes (vp9_webm)

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs`, branch `codecs`. Nothing committed.

## What happened with V10 (the STOP)

- **The row as specced.** V10 imports V1's file (640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm`). It puts the media alone in a 640 × 360 project and renders t = 3 s with `render_frame`, then compares each RGB channel's mean absolute difference with A1's project rendered at 3 s. The bound is 8/255.
- **What it read on Debug.** R 11.826, G 0.782, B 5.647. The two durations and sizes were right: 5.013 s, 640 × 360, with audio.
- **Sample pixels** (row 100, the colour bars). Each pair is source, then import:
  - cyan (0,255,255) → (23,255,255)
  - magenta (255,0,255) → (236,0,247)
  - green (0,255,1) → (20,255,9)
  - red (255,0,0) → (235,0,2)
- **The cause.** BT.709 cyan (Y′ 0.7874, Cr′ −0.5) decoded with BT.601's 1.402 gives R = 0.0864, which is 22. That is the import's 23, so the copy is being decoded as BT.601.
- **The control.** The same round trip at 1280 × 720 (a scratch script, same app, same AV.mov) reads R/G/B 0.526/0.157/0.296. Only the SD-sized picture is affected, which fits AVFoundation choosing the matrix by size for an unlabelled description.
- **Why I did not fix it.**
  - `ContainerRewrapWriter.labels` is reached only from `pqLabels` and `hlgLabels`. Its comment and spec §11 HD-18 (b) say "No other copy's description changes."
  - Labelling SDR copies by their Colour (primaries 1 and matrix 1 → BT.709) would change a §11 decision.
  - It would touch every SDR WebM/MKV import, not only Frame Job's own files.
  - Moving V10 to an HD canvas would make the row pass while the defect stays. That defect is any SD BT.709 VP9 WebM, from Frame Job or from ffmpeg, previewing with BT.601 colours.
- **Options for the orchestrator / owner:**
  - (a) A new §11 entry amending HD-18 (b): an SDR copy whose Colour names its primaries and matrix gets `ColorPrimaries` and `YCbCrMatrix`, and perhaps the 709 transfer, in its description. This is a change to `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift`, plus re-running the import proofs (`container_import_proof.py`, `codec_import_proof.py`, `hdr_proof.py`'s H7 rows). V10 then passes as written.
  - (b) Accept the defect, file it as an issue, and move V10's render comparison to a 1280 × 720 project (measured 0.53/0.16/0.30). The import half stays at 640 × 360.

# RULING-1 (orchestrator, 2026-10-28): V10's STOP

**Option (a). Fix the import, in this phase.** This is a real defect: any SD-sized SDR WebM/Matroska file labelled BT.709 imports with BT.601 colours. It isn't a product trade-off. It is in scope because C4's own acceptance ("Frame Job re-imports and previews its own VP9 WebM") depends on it, and the owner's standing rule is to do residue now rather than file it.

1. **Decision first.** Add a §11 entry that amends HD-18 (b) and HD-19 (b) before any code:
   - a rewrapped copy whose source states an SDR colour also gets its colour labels;
   - give the entry its own ID in `hdr.md`'s series (next free HD-n), or make it a CX-16 item, whichever its index already houses; "Amended by" lines on HD-18 and HD-19, and index rows.
   - The PQ/HLG rules stay exactly as they are.
2. **The rule, in this order of sources:**
   - **The Matroska Colour element.** Write its MatrixCoefficients, Primaries and TransferCharacteristics as the copy's `YCbCrMatrix` / `ColorPrimaries` / `TransferFunction`, but only for values AVFoundation has a constant for: 709, 601 (5/6) and 2020 matrices and primaries, and 709/sRGB-class transfers. Leave any value without one unwritten; do not guess.
   - **Otherwise, for VP9, the first keyframe's `color_space`.** The index already reads that header. A CS_BT_709 gives a BT.709 matrix, CS_BT_601/SMPTE_170 gives 601, CS_BT_2020 gives 2020; CS_UNKNOWN or anything else writes nothing.
   - **Neither present:** the copy is unchanged, as today.
   - Whichever you choose, the core publishes the values through `describe` (`container_codec.rs` / `container.rs` already publish `transfer`, `primaries` and `matrix`), and only Swift writes the labels.
3. **Proof:**
   - V10 passes as written at 640 × 360.
   - Add one import row at SD in the import proof that owns rewrap labels: a BT.709-labelled SD WebM imports at BT.709 and an unlabelled one is byte-identical to before.
   - Add one mutant: the SDR labelling dropped, caught on exactly those rows (V10 and the new row).
   - Re-run `container_import_proof.py`, `codec_import_proof.py` and `hdr_proof.py`'s H7 rows. Every earlier result must hold. A file now labelled where it was not, and rendering differently, is a finding to report, not to pin.
4. **Line caps.** If `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` or a core module is at its cap, make a pure move first, gated alone, as the rule says.
5. **Then carry on with the rest of 03-spec-final.md** and everything listed as owed in 04-impl-notes.md:
   - the 10-bit calibration column, the real VP9 table, P1, the `VP9MAX` placeholders and the catalog descriptions;
   - the index cells, the C4 record (with this ruling, the defect it fixed and its measurements) and the README section;
   - the nine mutants plus `av1-not-hdr`;
   - the offset rows, `make gate`, and the Release proofs.
6. **Your three mutant-row deviations are accepted** (`sdr-at-10-bits` +V8, `transfer-unlabelled` HLG/PQ only, `speed-on-vp9` +S1). Record each in the impl notes with its reason.
7. **Product STOP still applies.** If the 10-bit column cannot reach `hevc_10bit` under the cap, STOP for the owner, as the spec says.

Update 04-impl-notes.md (replace the STOP with the outcome) and 04-checks.txt.

 * A track is null when the file has none or none of its frames. `fourcc`

 * Blocks and no DefaultDuration, so its frames have no times", …). Freed
 * with `rc_container_free`. */
RcContainer *rc_container_open(const char *path, char **err_out);

def ebml_id(data, at):
    """An EBML element ID at `at`, its length marker kept: (id, the next offset)."""
    n = 9 - data[at].bit_length()
    if not 1 <= n <= 4 or at + n > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f"an element ID at {at} cannot be read")
    return int.from_bytes(data[at:at + n], "big"), at + n


def ebml_size(data, at):
    """An EBML size at `at`: (size, or None when unknown, the next offset)."""
    n = 9 - data[at].bit_length()
    if not 1 <= n <= 8 or at + n > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f"a size at {at} cannot be read")
    value = int.from_bytes(data[at:at + n], "big") & ((1 << (7 * n)) - 1)
    return (None if value == (1 << (7 * n)) - 1 else value), at + n


def ebml_children(data):
    """A master element's body as [(id, body)]; every child must have a size."""
    out, at = [], 0
    while at < len(data):
        eid, at = ebml_id(data, at)
        size, at = ebml_size(data, at)
        if size is None or at + size > len(data):
            raise ValueError(f"element {eid:X} has no size or runs past its parent")
        out.append((eid, data[at:at + size]))
        at += size
    return out


def ebml_element(eid, body):
    """`body` under `eid` with the shortest size that holds it (RFC 8794 §4)."""
    n = 1
    while len(body) >= (1 << (7 * n)) - 1:
        n += 1
    return (eid.to_bytes((eid.bit_length() + 7) // 8, "big")
            + (len(body) | (1 << (7 * n))).to_bytes(n, "big") + body)



def webm_fixture(name):
    """H7w's fixture: the ramp as VP9 Profile 2 `-lossless 1` (ffmpeg's libvpx-vp9, its
    WebM's Colour from the tags), rewritten with WEBM_FIXTURES' HDR10 children; kept only
    when ffprobe reads its tags and, in its stream side data, exactly those values."""
    tagset, max_cll, max_fall, luminance_max = {**WEBM_FIXTURES, **HLG_WEBM}[name]
    trc, primaries, space = WEBM_TAGS[tagset]
    out = MEDIA / f"{name}.webm"
    if not out.exists():
        raw = pq_raw()
        if raw is None:
            REFUSED[name] = REFUSED.get("base") or "ramp420p10.yuv was not made"
            return None
        # The tags on the input too: on the output alone ffmpeg 9.0.2 wrote the matrix
        # but not the transfer or primaries (measured), as with libsvtav1.
        tags = ["-color_range", "tv", "-color_trc", trc, "-color_primaries", primaries,
                "-colorspace", space]
        plain = ffmpeg_make(MEDIA / f"vp9_{tagset}.webm", [
            "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", "-s", f"{W}x{H}", "-framerate", "30",
            *tags, "-i", str(raw), "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-lossless", "1", "-profile:v", "2",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", *tags, "-write_crc32", "0"], 300)
        if plain is None:
            REFUSED[name] = f"ffmpeg did not make vp9_{tagset}.webm"
            return None
        try:
            webm_rewrite(plain, out, webm_colour_extra(max_cll, max_fall, luminance_max))
        except (ValueError, IndexError, OSError) as error:
            REFUSED[name] = f"{name}: the rewrite failed ({error})"
            out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            return None
    kept = checked(name, out, {"codec_name": "vp9", "pix_fmt": "yuv420p10le",
                               "color_transfer": trc, "color_primaries": primaries,

    if kept is None:

        return None
    return kept

def ebml_id(data, at):
    """An EBML element ID at `at`, its length marker kept: (id, the next offset)."""
    n = 9 - data[at].bit_length()
    if not 1 <= n <= 4 or at + n > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f"an element ID at {at} cannot be read")
    return int.from_bytes(data[at:at + n], "big"), at + n


def ebml_size(data, at):
    """An EBML size at `at`: (size, or None when unknown, the next offset)."""
    n = 9 - data[at].bit_length()
    if not 1 <= n <= 8 or at + n > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f"a size at {at} cannot be read")
    value = int.from_bytes(data[at:at + n], "big") & ((1 << (7 * n)) - 1)
    return (None if value == (1 << (7 * n)) - 1 else value), at + n


def ebml_children(data):
    """A master element's body as [(id, body)]; every child must have a size."""
    out, at = [], 0
    while at < len(data):
        eid, at = ebml_id(data, at)
        size, at = ebml_size(data, at)
        if size is None or at + size > len(data):
            raise ValueError(f"element {eid:X} has no size or runs past its parent")
        out.append((eid, data[at:at + size]))
        at += size
    return out


def ebml_element(eid, body):
    """`body` under `eid` with the shortest size that holds it (RFC 8794 §4)."""
    n = 1
    while len(body) >= (1 << (7 * n)) - 1:
        n += 1
    return (eid.to_bytes((eid.bit_length() + 7) // 8, "big")
            + (len(body) | (1 << (7 * n))).to_bytes(n, "big") + body)



def webm_fixture(name):
    """H7w's fixture: the ramp as VP9 Profile 2 `-lossless 1` (ffmpeg's libvpx-vp9, its
    WebM's Colour from the tags), rewritten with WEBM_FIXTURES' HDR10 children; kept only
    when ffprobe reads its tags and, in its stream side data, exactly those values."""
    tagset, max_cll, max_fall, luminance_max = {**WEBM_FIXTURES, **HLG_WEBM}[name]
    trc, primaries, space = WEBM_TAGS[tagset]
    out = MEDIA / f"{name}.webm"
    if not out.exists():
        raw = pq_raw()
        if raw is None:
            REFUSED[name] = REFUSED.get("base") or "ramp420p10.yuv was not made"
            return None
        # The tags on the input too: on the output alone ffmpeg 9.0.2 wrote the matrix
        # but not the transfer or primaries (measured), as with libsvtav1.
        tags = ["-color_range", "tv", "-color_trc", trc, "-color_primaries", primaries,
                "-colorspace", space]
        plain = ffmpeg_make(MEDIA / f"vp9_{tagset}.webm", [
            "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", "-s", f"{W}x{H}", "-framerate", "30",
            *tags, "-i", str(raw), "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-lossless", "1", "-profile:v", "2",
            "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", *tags, "-write_crc32", "0"], 300)
        if plain is None:
            REFUSED[name] = f"ffmpeg did not make vp9_{tagset}.webm"
            return None
        try:
            webm_rewrite(plain, out, webm_colour_extra(max_cll, max_fall, luminance_max))
        except (ValueError, IndexError, OSError) as error:
            REFUSED[name] = f"{name}: the rewrite failed ({error})"
            out.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            return None
    kept = checked(name, out, {"codec_name": "vp9", "pix_fmt": "yuv420p10le",
                               "color_transfer": trc, "color_primaries": primaries,
                               "color_space": space})
    if kept is None:
        return None
    read = side(kept, "stream")
    got = (fraction(read["mastering"]), fraction(read["cll"]))
    want = (luminance_max, max_cll)
    if got != want:
        REFUSED[name] = f"{name}: ffprobe reads mastering, MaxCLL {got}, not {want}"
        kept.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return None
    return kept

def av1_fixture(name):
    """P10's fixture: the ramp through libsvtav1, 10-bit, PQ-tagged in its sequence header
    and its MP4's `colr`, with AV1_FIXTURES' HDR10 metadata as metadata OBUs; kept only
    when ffprobe reads its tags, the values in its first frame's side data and no
    mastering or CLL in its stream side data (so the description carries neither)."""
    display, light = AV1_FIXTURES[name]
    out = MEDIA / f"{name}.mp4"
    if not out.exists():
        raw = pq_raw()
        if raw is None:
            REFUSED[name] = REFUSED.get("base") or "ramp420p10.yuv was not made"
            return None
        params = ["color-primaries=bt2020", "transfer-characteristics=smpte2084",
                  "matrix-coefficients=bt2020-ncl"]
        if display is not None:
            params.append(f"mastering-display={AV1_DISPLAY}L({display},0.005)")
        if light is not None:
            params.append(f"content-light={light[0]},{light[1]}")
        tags = ["-color_range", "tv", "-color_trc", "smpte2084", "-color_primaries", "bt2020",
                "-colorspace", "bt2020nc"]
        made = ffmpeg_make(out, [
            "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le", "-s", f"{W}x{H}", "-framerate", "30",
            *tags, "-i", str(raw), "-c:v", "libsvtav1", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p10le",
            "-preset", "8", "-svtav1-params", ":".join(params), *tags,
            "-movflags", "+write_colr"], 300)
        if made is None:
            REFUSED[name] = f"ffmpeg did not make {name}.mp4"
            return None
    kept = checked(name, out, {"codec_name": "av1", "pix_fmt": "yuv420p10le",
                               "color_transfer": "smpte2084", "color_primaries": "bt2020",
                               "color_space": "bt2020nc"})
    if kept is None:
        return None
    frame, stream_ = side(kept, "frame"), side(kept, "stream")
    got = (fraction(frame["mastering"]), fraction(frame["cll"]))
    want = (display, light[0] if light else None)
    if got != want or stream_ != {"mastering": None, "cll": None}:
        REFUSED[name] = (f"{name}: ffprobe reads mastering, MaxCLL {got} in the first frame "
                         f"(want {want}) and {stream_} in the stream")
        kept.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return None
    return kept


def av1_request():
    """P10's part of the probe's request: each AV1 fixture's path and what it must read."""
    items = []
    for name in AV1_FIXTURES:
        path = av1_fixture(name)
        item = {"name": name, "want": AV1_READS[name]}
        if path is None:
            item["why"] = REFUSED.get(name) or f"{name} was not made"
        else:
            item["path"] = str(path)
        items.append(item)
    return items

    """`path` alone at 1024×128: the media's `color` and `path` (the copy), and the
    render at T — peak_scene's shape plus `copy`; the doc is closed."""
    doc = Doc(client, f"w-{name}", W, H)
    doc.place(path) if doc.ok else None
    rows = doc.project().get("media") or [] if doc.ok else []
    color = rows[0].get("color") if rows else None
    copy = rows[0].get("path") if rows else None
    png = doc.render(f"w-{name}") if doc.ok else None
    closed = doc.close()
    source = yuv_frames(path, W, H)
    frame = Frame(png, W, H) if png else None
    if frame is None or not frame.ok or source is None or not closed or not copy:
        return {"why": f"{name}: {doc.why or 'no render, no copy, no decode or not closed'}",
                "color": color, "closed": closed}
    return {"color": color, "frame": frame, "source": source[0], "png": png, "closed": closed,

def colour_fields(path):

def run_h7w(client, state):
    """H7w (#316, spec §11 HD-18 (a), (b)): a VP9 WebM's Colour element gives import its
    PQ peak through the copy's description; an SDR WebM's HDR10 fields change nothing."""
    paths = {n: webm_fixture(n) for n in WEBM_FIXTURES}
    refused = {n: REFUSED.get(n) for n, p in paths.items() if p is None}
    state["h7w_fixture"] = not refused
    if refused:
        check("H7w the WebM fixtures were made", False, f"refused {refused}")
        return
    scenes = {n: webm_scene(client, n, p) for n, p in paths.items()}
    state["h7w_closed"] = all(s.get("closed") for s in scenes.values())
    misses, figures = [], []
    for n, want in WEBM_READS.items():
        color = scenes[n].get("color")
        if not isinstance(color, dict) or "pq" not in color:
            misses.append(f"CONTROL {n}: color {color}, so its copy does not read as PQ")
        elif color["pq"] != want:
            misses.append(f"{n}: color.pq {color['pq']}, want {want}")
        copy = scenes[n].get("copy")
        figures.append(f"{n}: color {color}; the copy's side data "
                       f"{side(copy, 'stream') if copy else scenes[n].get('why')}")
    for n, peak in (("pq_webm_cll", 600), ("pq_webm_display", 2000)):
        if "frame" not in scenes[n]:
            misses.append(scenes[n]["why"])
            continue
        worst = grey_misses(scenes[n], peak, n, misses)
        figures.append(f"{n}: worst |Δ| against the oracle at {peak} {worst} levels")
    sdr = [scenes["sdr_webm_cll"], scenes["sdr_webm_plain"]]
    for n in ("sdr_webm_cll", "sdr_webm_plain"):
        if scenes[n].get("color") is not None:
            misses.append(f"{n}: color {scenes[n]['color']}, want none")
    if any("copy" not in s for s in sdr):
        misses.extend(s["why"] for s in sdr if "copy" not in s)
    else:
        fields = [colour_fields(s["copy"]) for s in sdr]
        sides = [side(s["copy"], "stream") for s in sdr]
        figures.append(f"the SDR copies' colour fields {fields}, side data {sides}")
        if fields[0] != fields[1] or not fields[0]:
            misses.append(f"the SDR copies' colour fields differ: {fields}")
        if sides != [{"mastering": None, "cll": None}] * 2:
            misses.append(f"an SDR copy carries HDR10 side data: {sides}")
        if not same_png(sdr[0]["png"], sdr[1]["png"]):
            misses.append("the SDR copies' render_frame PNGs differ")
    check("H7w VP9 WebMs' Colour element: pq_webm_cll (MaxCLL 600, MaxFALL 200, mastering "
          "4,000) {600, max_cll}, pq_webm_display (mastering 2,000) {2000, mastering_display}, "
          "pq_webm_plain {} (CONTROL: each copy reads as PQ), their grey rows (every 8th "
          "column) = the oracle at 600/2000 ±1; sdr_webm_cll against sdr_webm_plain: no color, "
          "the copies' colour fields and side data equal (none), their renders byte-identical",
          not misses, f"failed {misses or 'none'}\n       " + "\n       ".join(figures))


def export_rgba(path, width, height, matrix, index=T // FRAME):
    """Frame `index` of an export decoded `yuva444p16le`: a function (x, y) → (straight
    R'G'B' through `matrix`, limited range, alpha), or None when it could not be read."""
    n = width * height
    size = 4 * n * 2
    raw = decode(path, "yuva444p16le", frames=index + 1)
    if not raw or len(raw) < size * (index + 1):
        return None
    values = struct.unpack(f"<{4 * n}H", raw[size * index:size * (index + 1)])

    def at(x, y):
        i = y * width + x
        luma, cb, cr, alpha = (values[k * n + i] for k in range(4))
        return rgb_of(luma / 64, cb / 64, cr / 64, matrix), alpha / 65535
    return at

def main():
    global selected
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("mode", nargs="?", choices=["capture", "compare"])
    parser.add_argument("folder", nargs="?")
    parser.add_argument("--app", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated rows to run and score")
    parser.add_argument("--measure", action="store_true", help="TI alone")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(MUTANTS) or None)
    parser.add_argument("--control", default=CONTROL)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode and not args.folder:
        print(f"{args.mode} needs a folder")
        return 2
    control = (ROOT / (args.folder or args.control)).resolve()
    if args.only:
        selected = {name.strip() for name in args.only.split(",") if name.strip()}
        unknown = selected - set(ROWS)
        if unknown:
            print(f"unknown rows: {sorted(unknown)}")
            return 2
    elif args.measure:
        selected = {"TI", "TH", "TO", "TL", "Z1"}
    else:
        selected -= {"TI", "TH", "TO", "TL"}
        if args.mutant:
            selected -= ({"H1a"} | H7_ROWS | H2_ROWS | H3_ROWS | H4_ROWS | L_ROWS | C2_ROWS
                         | C3_ROWS | B3_ROWS | B4_ROWS)
    if args.mode == "capture":
        if not args.only:
            selected = {"H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6", "R0", "Z1"}
        control.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.mode is None and not args.mutant:
        selected -= {"H1"}
    # Clean-up 3 batch B, phase 3 (#322): HG0 only captures, HGu only when `--only` names it,
    # and HG or HGk adds P15, whose answer HG reads.
    if args.mode != "capture":
        selected -= {"HG0"}
    if not args.only:
        selected -= {"HGu"}
    if selected & {"HG", "HGk"}:
        selected.add("P15")
    if "HGu" in selected:
        wanted = [p for paths in hg0_paths(control) for p in paths.values()]
        missing = next((p for p in wanted if not p.is_file()), None)
        if missing is not None:
            print(f"the control could not be performed — {missing} is missing")
            return 2
    remove_work()
    atexit.register(remove_work)
    HOME.mkdir(parents=True)
    named = MUTANTS[args.mutant][1] if args.mutant else []
    binary = Path(args.app) if args.app else proof_app.binary()
    if binary.suffix == ".app":
        binary = proof_app.executable(binary)
    sources = ROOT / "app/Sources"
    config = proof_app.config()
    if args.mutant:
        print(f"grading-3 T3-1 — the {args.mutant} MUTANT ({' '.join(named)} must FAIL)",
              flush=True)
        app, copy = build_mutant(args.mutant)
        if app is None:
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — {copy}")
            return 2
        binary = proof_app.executable(app)
        sources = copy / "app/Sources"
    else:
        what = args.mode or ("measure" if args.measure else "run")
        print(f"grading-3 T3-1 — honest sources over MCP ({what}, {config} build {binary})",
              flush=True)
    if not binary.is_file():
        print(f"instrument failure: no app binary at {binary}")
        return 2
    state = {}
    closed = True
    log = WORK / "instance.log"
    needs_instance = bool(selected & ({"H1", "H1m", "H1a", "H1s", "H1w", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5",
                                       "H6", "R0"} | H7_ROWS | H2_ROWS
                                      | (H3_ROWS - {"DX"}) | H4_ROWS | L_ROWS | C2_ROWS
                                      | C3_ROWS | B3_ROWS | B4_ROWS | {"P12", "P13", "P15"}))

def main():
    global selected
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("mode", nargs="?", choices=["capture", "compare"])
    parser.add_argument("folder", nargs="?")
    parser.add_argument("--app", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated rows to run and score")
    parser.add_argument("--measure", action="store_true", help="TI alone")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", choices=sorted(MUTANTS) or None)
    parser.add_argument("--control", default=CONTROL)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.mode and not args.folder:
        print(f"{args.mode} needs a folder")
        return 2
    control = (ROOT / (args.folder or args.control)).resolve()
    if args.only:
        selected = {name.strip() for name in args.only.split(",") if name.strip()}
        unknown = selected - set(ROWS)
        if unknown:
            print(f"unknown rows: {sorted(unknown)}")
            return 2
    elif args.measure:
        selected = {"TI", "TH", "TO", "TL", "Z1"}
    else:
        selected -= {"TI", "TH", "TO", "TL"}
        if args.mutant:
            selected -= ({"H1a"} | H7_ROWS | H2_ROWS | H3_ROWS | H4_ROWS | L_ROWS | C2_ROWS
                         | C3_ROWS | B3_ROWS | B4_ROWS)
    if args.mode == "capture":
        if not args.only:
            selected = {"H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5", "H6", "R0", "Z1"}
        control.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.mode is None and not args.mutant:
        selected -= {"H1"}
    # Clean-up 3 batch B, phase 3 (#322): HG0 only captures, HGu only when `--only` names it,
    # and HG or HGk adds P15, whose answer HG reads.
    if args.mode != "capture":
        selected -= {"HG0"}
    if not args.only:
        selected -= {"HGu"}
    if selected & {"HG", "HGk"}:
        selected.add("P15")
    if "HGu" in selected:
        wanted = [p for paths in hg0_paths(control) for p in paths.values()]
        missing = next((p for p in wanted if not p.is_file()), None)
        if missing is not None:
            print(f"the control could not be performed — {missing} is missing")
            return 2
    remove_work()
    atexit.register(remove_work)
    HOME.mkdir(parents=True)
    named = MUTANTS[args.mutant][1] if args.mutant else []
    binary = Path(args.app) if args.app else proof_app.binary()
    if binary.suffix == ".app":
        binary = proof_app.executable(binary)
    sources = ROOT / "app/Sources"
    config = proof_app.config()
    if args.mutant:
        print(f"grading-3 T3-1 — the {args.mutant} MUTANT ({' '.join(named)} must FAIL)",
              flush=True)
        app, copy = build_mutant(args.mutant)
        if app is None:
            print(f"mutant {args.mutant}: the control could not be performed — {copy}")
            return 2
        binary = proof_app.executable(app)
        sources = copy / "app/Sources"
    else:
        what = args.mode or ("measure" if args.measure else "run")
        print(f"grading-3 T3-1 — honest sources over MCP ({what}, {config} build {binary})",
              flush=True)
    if not binary.is_file():
        print(f"instrument failure: no app binary at {binary}")
        return 2
    state = {}
    closed = True
    log = WORK / "instance.log"
    needs_instance = bool(selected & ({"H1", "H1m", "H1a", "H1s", "H1w", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5",
                                       "H6", "R0"} | H7_ROWS | H2_ROWS
